Tensor Analysis – Practical 9 Solutions Information: • Please make sure to complete all exercises before the next lecture. • The exercises marked with [See lecture] were solved in class. • The exercises are not organised by difficulty. 9.1 Given a 2-dimensional metric tensor [gij] = ( 1 0 0 e2x ) for the a coordinate system (x1, x2) = (x, y), calculate the components of the Ricci tensor Rij. Solution: Let us find the Christoffel symbols of second kind. The only non-zero partial derivative ∂gik ∂xℓ is ∂g22 ∂x1 = ∂e2x ∂x = 2e2x. Thus, using the formula Γ i jk = 1 2 giℓ ( ∂gℓj ∂xk + ∂gℓk ∂xj − ∂gjk ∂xℓ ) , we see that the only possibly non-zero Christoffel symbols of second type are the ones having two indices 2 and one index 1. That is, Γ1 22, Γ2 12, and Γ2 21. Before computing the Christoffel symbols, we need to compute the inverse metric gij: [gij] = (1 0 0 e−2x ) Thus, Γ 1 11 = Γ 1 12 = Γ 1 21 = Γ 2 11 = Γ 2 22 = 0 1

4 9.2 Consider the 3-dimensional space in spherical coordinates that has arc length element ds2 = dr2 + r2dθ2 + r2 sin 2 θ dϕ2 Compute the Ricci tensor components Rkk for this coordinate system. Here (x1, x2, x3) = (r, θ, ϕ) Solution: We have [gij] =  1 0 0 0 r2 0 0 0 r2 sin 2 θ   Thus, the only non-zero partial derivative ∂gik ∂xℓ are ∂g22 ∂x1 = ∂r2 ∂r = 2r ∂g33 ∂x1 = ∂r2 sin 2 θ ∂r = 2r sin 2 θ ∂g33 ∂x2 = ∂r2 sin 2 θ ∂θ = 2r2 sin θ cos θ Thus, the only possible non-zero Christoffel symbols are the ones having two indices 2 and one index 1, the ones having two indices 3 and one index 1, and the ones having two indices 3 and one index 2. Before finding them, we still need [gij] =  1 0 0 0 1 r2 0 0 0 1 r2 sin2 θ   . Thus, using the formula Γ i jk = 1 2 giℓ ( ∂gℓj ∂xk + ∂gℓk ∂xj − ∂gjk ∂xℓ ) , we get that the non-zero Christoffel symbols are Γ 1 22 = r, Γ 1 33 = −r sin 2 θ Γ 2 12Γ2 21 = − 1 r , Γ2 33 = − sin θ cos θ Γ 3 13 = 1 r , Γ 3 23 = cot θ. Using the formula Rij = ∂Γk ij ∂xk − ∂Γk ik ∂xj + Γk ijΓl kℓ − Γ ℓ ikΓ k jℓ we can show that the Ricci tensor components are R11 = 0, R22 = 1, R33 = sin 2 θ.

5 9.3 Given a 3-dimensional metric tensor gij =  e2u 0 0 0 e2v 0 0 0 e2w   in coordinates (x1, x2, x3) = (u, v, w). Find the Ricci tensor components Rij. Solution: Again, gij =   e2u 0 0 0 e2v 0 0 0 e2w   . Thus, the only non-zero partial derivative ∂gik ∂xℓ are ∂g11 ∂x1 = ∂e2u ∂u = 2e 2u, ∂g22 ∂x2 = ∂e2v ∂v = 2e2v, ∂g33 ∂x3 = ∂e2w ∂w = 2e2w. Thus, the only possible non-zero Christoffel symbols are the ones having three repeated indices. Before computing these Christoffel symbols, we still need gij =   e−2u 0 0 0 e−2v 0 0 0 e−2w   . Thus, using the formula Γ i jk = 1 2 giℓ ( ∂gℓj ∂xk + ∂gℓk ∂xj − ∂gjk ∂xℓ ) , we get that the non-zero Christoffel symbols are Γ1 11 = 1 2 (e −2u)(2e2u) = 1, Γ2 22 = 1 2 (e −2v)(2e 2v) = 1, Γ3 33 = 1 2 (e −2w)(2e 2w) = 1.

Revision exercises 9.4 Consider the coordinate system having coordinates (x1, x2, x3) = (ϕ, θ, z) and position vector r = cos ϕ(sin θ + cos θ)i1 + sin ϕ(sin θ + cos θ)i2 + zi3, where i1, i2, i3 are the usual Cartesian basis vectors. (1) Find basis vectors e1, e2, e2. (2) Show that this is an orthogonal coordinate system. Solution: (1) To find the basis vectors e1, e2, e3 we use the formula ei = ∂r ∂xi . We have e1 = ∂r ∂x1 = ∂ ∂ϕ (cos ϕ(sin θ + cos θ)i1 + sin ϕ(sin θ + cos θ)i2 + zi3) = − sin ϕ(sin θ + cos θ)i1 + cos ϕ(sin θ + cos θ)i2, e2 = ∂r ∂x2 = ∂ ∂θ (cos ϕ(sin θ + cos θ)i1 + sin ϕ(sin θ + cos θ)i2 + zi3) = cos ϕ(cos θ − sin θ)i1 + sin ϕ(cos θ − sin θ)i2, e3 = ∂r ∂x3 = ∂ ∂ϕ (cos ϕ(sin θ + cos θ)i1 + sin ϕ(sin θ + cos θ)i2 + zi3) = i3.

Find the covariant components of the vector A = −i1 + i2 with respect to the basis e1, e2, e3 of Question 9.4. Solution: The covariant components of A are given by Ai = A · ei. Thus, A1 =   −1 1 0   ·   − sin ϕ(sin θ + cos θ) cos ϕ(sin θ + cos θ) 0   = sin ϕ(sin θ + cos θ) + cos ϕ(sin θ + cos θ) = (sin ϕ + cos ϕ)(sin θ + cos θ), A2 =  −1 1 0   ·   cos ϕ(cos θ − sin θ) sin ϕ(cos θ − sin θ) 0   = − cos ϕ(cos θ − sin θ) + sin ϕ(cos θ − sin θ) = (sin ϕ − cos ϕ)(cos θ − sin θ), A3 =  −1 1 0   ·  0 0 1   = 0.

9 the metric coefficients are h1 = sin θ + cos θ, h2 = cos θ − sin θ, h3 = 1. 9.7 Determine all Christoffel symbols of the first and of the second kind for the coordinate system of Question 9.4. Solution: In Question 9.6, we computed g11 = (sin θ + cos θ) 2, g22 = (cos θ − sin θ) 2, g33 = 1, hence g11 = 1 (sin θ + cos θ)2 , g22 = 1 (cos θ − sin θ)2 , g33 = 1. Thus, the only non-zero partial derivative ∂gik ∂xℓ are ∂g11 ∂x2 = ∂ ∂θ (sin θ + cos θ) 2 = 2(sin θ + cos θ)(cos θ − sin θ) = 2(cos 2 θ − sin 2 θ), ∂g22 ∂x2 = ∂ ∂θ (cos θ − sin θ) 2 = 2(cos θ − sin θ)(− sin θ − cos θ) = −2(cos2 θ − sin 2 θ) Analysing the formula Γijk = 1 2 ( ∂gik ∂xj + ∂gij ∂xk − ∂gkj ∂xi ) we conclude that the only possibly non-zero Christoffel symbols of first kind are the ones having two indices 1 and one index 2 or three indices 2. Let us compute the non-zero Christoffel symbols of first kind. Γ211 = 1 2 ( ∂g21 ∂x1 + ∂g21 ∂x1 − ∂g11 ∂x2 ) = − 1 2 ∂g11 ∂x2 = − 1 2 2(cos2 θ − sin 2 θ) = sin 2 θ − cos2 θ Γ222 = 1 2 ( ∂g22 ∂x2 + ∂g22 ∂x2 − ∂g22 ∂x2 ) = 1 2 ( ∂g22 ∂x2 ) = 1 2 (−2(cos2 θ − sin 2 θ)) = sin 2 θ − cos2 θ. Using Ricci’s Theorem, we get Γ211 + Γ121 = ∂g21 ∂x1 = 0, Thus, Γ121 = −Γ211 = cos 2 θ − sin 2 θ.
